title: Anchor R&D Control Surface — Master Plan (frozen design)
claims: This planning session ran Crucible over the Anchor codebase on 2026-06-07 and 06-08 and produced a frozen, Foreman-ready design for turning Anchor from a task and project tracker into a per-project R&D control surface. The locked North Star treats each code project as a folder, with a single dashboard window that drives the researchPrime → Crucible → Foreman trio as durable, server-owned Claude Code jobs on gwl-server, complete with versioned effort history, task-to-project linking, project lifecycle states, deliverable execution, and a data-free public distribution. The session settled the core architecture around one uniform job primitive: every lane is the same `claude -p` stream-json invocation running the relevant skill in the project's working directory, owned by the Anchor server, with no per-lane orchestration, no PTY, and stdlib only. Skill gates such as AskUserQuestion are handled in-session by surfacing the structured question in the stream and sending the user's choice back as a plain text turn. Alongside those design decisions, the user locked several scope and infrastructure choices: a brownfield extension of the existing Anchor repo, a streaming console rather than a full TUI, a new parallel R&D registry distinct from life-domain projects, artifacts stored as pointer-records inside each project's `.anchor/` folder, all three trio lanes on Claude Code CLI only with Gemini deferred, the Anchor service running as the `john` user to clear the LocalSystem credential wall, and remote access via the Tailscale interface with a shared-secret token on mutating API calls. The session delivered four documents: the Master Plan capturing the frozen design, the Implementation Plan ready for Foreman to build, a Decision Log recording each decision and the adversarial Shark-Tank findings that drove it, and an Execution Log tracking the run itself.
